construction_note: All values placed within published distribution bands from the references below. Population sources do not provide named-cohort means; values within each persona are illustrative points inside the cited bands, not point estimates from a specific table. Selected to span the actual US adult distribution across activity level, age, sex, and sleep pattern.

references.ostchega_2011: Ostchega Y, Porter KS, Hughes J, Dillon CF, Nwankwo T. Resting pulse rate reference data for children, adolescents, and adults: United States, 1999-2008. Natl Health Stat Report. 2011;(41):1-16. PMID: 21905522. Adult mean RPR 72 bpm; max ~92 bpm.
references.avram_2019: Avram R, Tison GH, Aschbacher K, et al. Real-world heart rate norms in the Health eHeart study. NPJ Digit Med. 2019;2:58. doi:10.1038/s41746-019-0134-9. n=92,457 US adults; mean real-world HR 79.1 ± 14.5 bpm; women ~4 bpm higher than men.
references.reimers_2018: Reimers AK, Knapp G, Reimers CD. Effects of exercise on the resting heart rate: A systematic review and meta-analysis of interventional studies. J Clin Med. 2018;7(12):503. PMC6306777. Endurance athletes typical RHR 40-60 bpm; elite as low as 30 bpm.
references.bassett_2010: Bassett DR Jr, Wyatt HR, Thompson H, Peters JC, Hill JO. Pedometer-measured physical activity in U.S. adults. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2010;42(10):1819-1825. NHANES 2005-2006 accelerometer (n=3744 adults ≥20y): mean 9,676 uncensored / 6,540 censored steps/day.
references.tudor_locke_2011: Tudor-Locke C, Craig CL, Brown WJ, et al. How many steps/day are enough? For adults. Int J Behav Nutr Phys Act. 2011;8:79. Step-defined zones: <5000 sedentary, 5000-7499 low active, 7500-9999 somewhat active, 10000-12499 active, ≥12500 highly active.
references.tudor_locke_2013_older: Tudor-Locke C, Schuna JM Jr, Barreira TV, et al. Normative steps/day values for older adults: NHANES 2005-2006. J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci. 2013. PMID: 23913932. Sex-and-age-specific norms for adults 60+.
references.sisson_2012: Sisson SB, Camhi SM, Tudor-Locke C, et al. Characteristics of step-defined physical activity categories in U.S. adults. Am J Health Promot. 2012;26(3):152-159. US adult distribution: 36.1% sedentary, 47.6% low-to-somewhat-active, 16.3% active-to-highly-active.
references.nhis_2020_sleep: Adjaye-Gbewonyo D, Ng AE, Black LI. QuickStats: Percentage of adults aged ≥18 years who sleep <7 hours, by sex and age group — NHIS 2020. MMWR Morb Mortal Wkly Rep. 2022;71(10):393. DOI: 10.15585/mmwr.mm7110a6. M 18-44: 28.8% <7h; F 18-44: 25.6%; M 45-64: 31.1%; F 45-64: 30.7%; M 65+: 22.6%; F 65+: 25.5%.
references.nhanes_2007_2010_sleep: Frenk SM, Chong Y. QuickStats: Sleep duration among adults aged ≥20 years, by race/ethnicity — NHANES 2007-2010. MMWR. 2013. 60.4% slept 7-9h; 37.3% slept ≤6h; 2.3% slept ≥10h.
references.brfss_2020_sleep: Pankowska MM, Lu H, Wheaton AG, et al. Prevalence and geographic patterns of self-reported short sleep duration among US adults, 2020. Prev Chronic Dis. 2023;20:E53. PMID: 37384831. 33.2% of adults report <7h.
references.shockey_2017_shift: Shockey TM, Wheaton AG. Short sleep duration by occupation group — 29 states, 2013-2014. MMWR Morb Mortal Wkly Rep. 2017;66(8):207-213. PMC5657897. Shift work occupations show significantly elevated short-sleep prevalence vs day workers.
references.cdc_pa_guidelines_2018: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition. 2018. Adults: 150-300 min/wk moderate-intensity OR 75-150 min/wk vigorous-intensity aerobic, plus muscle-strengthening 2+ days/wk.
references.cdc_pa_2024: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. National Health Interview Survey 2024. 47.2% of US adults met the aerobic physical activity guideline (52.3% men, 42.4% women).

personas.label: sedentary office worker, M, age 28-32
personas.narrative_summary: Desk-bound during work hours with minimal structured exercise. Walks for errands but rarely hits a full hour of intentional activity in a week.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Within ostchega_2011 adult range (mean 72, max ~92); plausible for sedentary younger adult per avram_2019 real-world distribution.
source_notes.steps_daily_avg: Tudor-Locke 'sedentary' band (<5000); matches sisson_2012 finding that 36.1% of US adults fall in this band.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within short-sleep band (<7h); nhis_2020_sleep reports 28.8% of men 18-44 sleep <7h.
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Below cdc_pa_guidelines_2018 150-min threshold; consistent with the ~48% of men not meeting aerobic guideline (cdc_pa_2024).

personas.label: casual runner, F, age 25-29
personas.narrative_summary: Logs 3 weekday morning runs of 30-45 minutes plus a weekend long run. Sleep is decent because she protects an 11pm bedtime.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Within trained-recreational range; avram_2019 reports women 18-44 middle 50% spans roughly 62-78 bpm with lower values among regular exercisers.
source_notes.steps_daily_avg: tudor_locke_2011 'somewhat active' band (7500-9999); higher end consistent with sub-elite runner.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhanes_2007_2010_sleep 7-9h healthy range (60.4% of adults).
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Exceeds cdc_pa_guidelines_2018 150-min moderate threshold; within 150-300 recommended range.
source_notes.workout_sessions_weekly: Meets aerobic frequency expected for cdc_pa_2024 guideline-meeters.

personas.label: competitive cyclist, M, age 34-38
personas.narrative_summary: Trains 10-12 hours per week on a polarized model — most volume easy, threshold work midweek, hard group rides on weekends.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Within reimers_2018 endurance-athlete range (40-60 bpm); typical for trained but non-elite competitive cyclist.
source_notes.steps_daily_avg: tudor_locke_2011 'somewhat active'; cyclists accumulate less step volume than runners due to cycling not generating steps.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhanes_2007_2010_sleep healthy range; serious recreational athletes commonly prioritize sleep.
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Far exceeds cdc_pa_guidelines_2018 vigorous threshold (75-150 min); consistent with 10+ hr/wk training volume.
source_notes.workout_sessions_weekly: Daily training pattern common in cycling at this volume.

personas.label: masters marathoner, F, age 38-42
personas.narrative_summary: Marathon training block of 50+ miles per week across 5-6 runs. Long run Sunday, quality day midweek, easy aerobic the rest.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Within reimers_2018 endurance-trained range (40-60); females typically 3-5 bpm above male equivalent per avram_2019.
source_notes.steps_daily_avg: tudor_locke_2011 'active' band (10000-12499); appropriate for 50mi/wk training volume.
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Substantially exceeds cdc_pa_guidelines_2018; consistent with marathon training block.
source_notes.workout_sessions_weekly: Typical for masters marathon training; reimers_2018 references endurance athlete training frequency.

personas.label: new parent, low sleep, M, age 30-34
personas.narrative_summary: Activity dropped after his second kid. Sleep is fragmented across nights — total time in bed is fine but consolidated sleep is short.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Matches ostchega_2011 NHANES adult mean (72 bpm); typical for moderately-active middle-young male.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhis_2020_sleep short-sleep band; 28.8% of men 18-44 report <7h, sleep fragmentation common in early parenthood.
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Below cdc_pa_guidelines_2018 150-min threshold; consistent with reduced volume in parenting years.
source_notes.workout_sessions_weekly: Partial adherence to aerobic guideline; no muscle-strengthening compliance.

personas.label: retired, active walker, F, age 62-68
personas.narrative_summary: Walks 45-60 minutes most mornings, twice-weekly water aerobics, weekend hikes when weather is good.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Within ostchega_2011 older-adult range; modest age-related elevation moderated by regular activity.
source_notes.steps_daily_avg: tudor_locke_2013_older 'somewhat active' for adults 60+ exceeding median.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhis_2020_sleep healthy range; women 65+ less likely to be short sleepers (25.5% <7h).
source_notes.workout_sessions_weekly: Daily-walking + water-aerobics pattern; meets muscle-strengthening with aerobics.

personas.label: college student, irregular schedule, M, age 19-22
personas.narrative_summary: Inconsistent week-to-week — exam weeks crash to near-sedentary, off-weeks include 3-4 pickup-basketball or gym sessions. Sleep schedule is chaotic.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Within ostchega_2011 young-adult range; younger adults trend slightly higher real-world per avram_2019.
source_notes.steps_daily_avg: tudor_locke_2011 'low active' band; college campuses generate moderate ambient walking.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhis_2020_sleep short-sleep band common in 18-44; college populations skew toward short, irregular sleep.
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Just below cdc_pa_guidelines_2018 150-min threshold; reflects week-to-week variability.
source_notes.workout_sessions_weekly: Partial adherence; recreational rather than structured.

personas.label: CrossFit regular, F, age 28-33
personas.narrative_summary: Five class sessions weekly mixing strength, conditioning, and Olympic lifts. Adds easy zone-2 cardio on rest days for recovery.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Lower bound of reimers_2018 trained-recreational range; appropriate for HIIT/strength-trained female.
source_notes.steps_daily_avg: tudor_locke_2011 'somewhat active'; CrossFit doesn't generate huge step counts but lifestyle is active.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhanes_2007_2010_sleep healthy range; serious recreational athletes often prioritize sleep.
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Exceeds cdc_pa_guidelines_2018 150-300 min range; supports high-volume training.

personas.label: shift worker, disrupted sleep, M, age 40-46
personas.narrative_summary: Rotating swing shifts disrupt sleep onset and duration. Activity is mostly on-the-clock walking; structured exercise rarely fits in.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Slightly elevated within ostchega_2011 adult range; chronic short sleep associated with elevated RHR per avram_2019.
source_notes.steps_daily_avg: tudor_locke_2011 'low active'; manual-occupation walking contributes most volume.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within short-sleep band; shockey_2017_shift documents elevated short-sleep prevalence in shift-work occupations; nhis_2020_sleep 31.1% of men 45-64 sleep <7h.
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Below cdc_pa_guidelines_2018 150-min threshold; shift schedules complicate structured exercise.
source_notes.workout_sessions_weekly: Does not meet aerobic or muscle-strengthening guideline frequency.

personas.label: yoga + hiking, F, age 45-52
personas.narrative_summary: Three yoga classes plus 1-2 longer hikes weekly. Lifts light weights twice a week. Sleep is consistent thanks to a stable bedtime.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Within avram_2019 active-female-midlife range; moderate aerobic conditioning.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhis_2020_sleep healthy range; women 45-64 30.7% <7h, so this persona is in the 69% who meet guideline.
